newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends lower after making new highs.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends lower after making new highs.

text.p: CSCE world sugar was sharply lower midsession Friday, after a break back below two week old support levels led funds to take profits on the recent rally, traders said.

"Yesterday's action - a new high, but a lower close - was bearish and when the market gapped lower on the open and broke support around 11.50 cents (basis October), the funds just stomped all over it," one broker said.
CSCE October sugar was down 0.17 cent at 11.41 cents late morning, after seeing a morning low at 11.32 cents, the lowest level since July 22.

Daily momentum indicators were now giving bearish signals, but the contract's five-day moving average was still above 21-day average, and above its 55-day average, suggesting the slow uptrend in place for most of the year was still intact, analysts said.

In slightly bearish news overnight for the global sugar market, the first beet test results from the Ukraine suggested crop prospects are much better than last year, according to industry statisician, F.O. Licht.
But the El Nino global weather pattern may yet reduce supplies and Australian sugar exports in June, fell to 154,703 tonnes raw against 172,991 tonnes in June last year.
Overall the impact of the El Nino phenomenon is to bring dry weather to Australia and South East Asia, resulting in smaller sugar cane crops.
But in the longer term the sugar market is anticipating that the global build up of world stocks will slow or even decline this year, as output stabilizes after two years of rises, analysts said.
Already this season, the Indian crop is about 30 percent smaller, though India has huge stockpiles of sugar.
